docs.title: Pourpoint
docs.text:
Pourpoint is a Python package for delineating watersheds from existing hydrofabrics. A watershed is the area of land that drains to a particular outlet. A hydrofabric represents that landscape as connected sub-basins and rivers, sometimes accompanied by flow-direction and flow-accumulation rasters.

Starting from a point, Pourpoint follows those connections upstream to collect the contributing sub-basins. Where rasters are available, it can refine the watershed cell by cell to resolve the land draining to the chosen outlet. You can work with the resulting geometries in Python or export them with the river network to a portable QGIS project.

Pourpoint reads hydrofabrics through HydroFabric Exchange (HFX), which packages their geometries, connections, attributes and available rasters. The concepts guide explains how these pieces fit together, from a point watershed to the upstream contributing area of a region.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.13 or later. With uv, add Pourpoint to your project.

uv add pourpoint

You can also install it with pip install pourpoint.

docs.title: Delineate the Rhine at Basel
docs.text:
The point at 47.5596° N, 7.5890° E lies on the Rhine in Basel, Switzerland. We will use the public GRIT hydrofabric to find its watershed and save a QGIS project. Pourpoint reads the required data from the hosted HFX bundle, so this example needs an internet connection.

A point chosen on a map can fall slightly beside the hydrofabric's river line. We first select nearby rivers and snap the point to the nearest segment within 100 metres. Coordinates use longitude followed by latitude.

from shapely.geometry import Point, box

import pourpoint as pp


dataset = "https://basin-delineations-public.upstream.tech/grit/hfx-v0.4.0/"
point = Point(7.5890, 47.5596)

with pp.HydroFabric(dataset) as fabric:
    nearby_rivers = pp.select_rivers(
        fabric=fabric,
        target=box(7.5790, 47.5496, 7.5990, 47.5696),
    )
    outlet = pp.snap(target=point, onto=nearby_rivers, radius=100)

    # Follow the sub-basin connections upstream from the outlet.
    subbasins = pp.select_upstream_subbasins(fabric=fabric, target=outlet)

    # Use native flow rasters to resolve the watershed within those sub-basins.
    refined = pp.refine(fabric=fabric, target=outlet, subbasins=subbasins)
    watershed = pp.merge(subbasins=refined.subbasins)

    # Select the supplied rivers inside the refined watershed.
    rivers = pp.select_rivers(fabric=fabric, target=watershed)

    bundle = pp.QGISBundle()
    bundle.add_result(refined)
    bundle.add_vector("watershed", watershed, crs="EPSG:4326")
    bundle.add_vector("rivers", rivers)
    bundle.add_vector("requested_point", point, crs="EPSG:4326")
    bundle.write("rhine-basel")

The code above generates the watershed shown below.

Open rhine-basel/watershed.qgz in QGIS. The folder contains the vector layers and native raster subsets alongside the project. Keep the folder together when moving or sharing it, and choose a new output folder for each export.

Boundaries: Natural Earth. Their depiction implies no position on territorial status.

docs.title: Use the combined workflow
docs.text:
When you only need the final result, delineate combines snapping, upstream selection, refinement and merging. Using the same imports, dataset and point, the following produces the same watershed and river geometries in a second bundle.

with pp.HydroFabric(dataset) as fabric:
    nearby_rivers = pp.select_rivers(
        fabric=fabric,
        target=box(7.5790, 47.5496, 7.5990, 47.5696),
    )
    result = pp.delineate(
        fabric=fabric,
        target=point,
        snap_onto=nearby_rivers,
        radius=100,
        refine=True,
    )
    rivers = pp.select_rivers(fabric=fabric, target=result.subbasins)

    bundle = pp.QGISBundle()
    bundle.add_result(result)
    bundle.add_vector("rivers", rivers)
    bundle.add_vector("requested_point", point, crs="EPSG:4326")
    bundle.write("rhine-basel-combined")

add_result includes the merged watershed, individual sub-basin contributions, outlet cell and raster subsets. River selection remains a separate step, so you can choose which network to include.

docs.title: Hydrofabrics: the datasets Pourpoint operates on
docs.text:
A hydrofabric describes how a landscape drains. The USGS defines it as “a dataset containing a network of connected representations of rivers, lakes, and catchments” (USGS, Progress Toward a Reference Hydrologic Geospatial Fabric).

In Pourpoint, we understand a hydrofabric as a dataset tiling the landscape into sub-basins, describing their downstream connections, and providing the river network alongside auxiliary data, when available, such as the flow-direction and flow-accumulation rasters used to produce it.

Pourpoint operates on these existing datasets; it does not construct the hydrofabric from elevation data. It reads them through HydroFabric Exchange (HFX), the format that packages their geometries, connectivity, attributes and available rasters. Examples of such datasets include GRIT, MERIT-Basins, derived from MERIT Hydro, and TDX-Hydro.

docs.title: Delineating a watershed from a point
docs.text: In Pourpoint, we understand a watershed as the area of land that drains to a specified outlet point.

docs.title: Snap the point to a river
docs.text:
A hydrofabric represents rivers with vector lines. Those lines simplify the river's course and may not coincide exactly with a surveyed location or a point chosen on a map. A point intended to represent a river outlet can therefore fall beside the dataset's river line.

We recommend snapping the requested point to the hydrofabric's river network, especially when raster refinement will follow. Snapping places the point on the nearest supplied river segment within a search radius. It helps align the request with the dataset's representation of drainage; refinement will then search nearby for an outlet cell. See snap for the operation and its parameters.

Snapping is optional: Pourpoint can also delineate from the original point. We use \(p\) for the point after snapping, or for the unchanged point when snapping is not requested. In the first panel below, \(p\) lies on the river network.

Locate the point, identify its terminal sub-basin, then select the sub-basins upstream of it. Conceptual schematic.

docs.title: Identify the terminal unit
docs.text:
Pourpoint locates the sub-basin containing \(p\). This is the starting place for our upstream search, and we call it the terminal unit, denoted by \(t\). The second panel highlights it in blue. If \(p\) lies exactly on a shared boundary, we need a way to choose between the touching sub-basins: Pourpoint arbitrarily assigns it to the one whose numerical ID is smallest.

We use \(b\) for a sub-basin and \(P_b\) for its polygon. In particular, \(t\) is the sub-basin associated with our point \(p\), and \(P_t\) is its polygon.

docs.title: Collect upstream sub-basins
docs.text:
Starting at \(t\), follow the hydrofabric's connections upstream. First find the sub-basins draining directly into \(t\), then those draining into them, and continue until no new sub-basins remain. The third panel shows the selected units, including \(t\) itself.

Mathematically, we write \(b \to t\) when sub-basin \(b\) drains directly into \(t\), and \(b \to^* t\) when it reaches \(t\) through any number of downstream connections. We allow zero connections, so \(t \to^* t\). The selected set is

\[ \mathcal B_t = \{b \mid b \to^* t\}. \]

Here \(b\) denotes a sub-basin, and the arrow describes the hydrofabric's connectivity between sub-basins. Thus \(\mathcal B_t\) contains \(t\) and every sub-basin that drains into it, directly or indirectly.

Combining their polygons gives the vector footprint:

\[ M = \bigcup_{b \in \mathcal B_t} P_b. \]

The union symbol means combine the polygons of all selected sub-basins, counting overlapping land once. This is the result of select_upstream_subbasins, which also forms the vector-selection stage of delineate.

docs.title: Refining a point watershed
docs.text:
No matter where \(p\) lies within its terminal unit, vector delineation selects the same sub-basins and produces the same footprint. The figure below illustrates why this can include land that does not drain to the requested point.

Left: vector footprint. Right: raster-refined footprint. Conceptual schematic. The terminal polygon is labelled \(P_s\) in this figure; it corresponds to \(P_t\) in the text.

In the left panel, both upstream units \(u_1\) and \(u_2\) drain into the terminal unit. However, \(p\) lies on the left branch, above the junction. Water from \(u_2\) joins that branch downstream of \(p\), so it does not drain to \(p\). Selecting whole sub-basins includes \(u_2\) because it drains to the terminal unit, not because it drains to the particular point we chose inside it.

Even a point on the main stem can lie upstream of the sub-basin's declared outlet, labelled \(q\). Land draining into the river between that point and \(q\) also belongs to the vector footprint but not to the point's watershed.

This is where sub-basin size matters. We can informally think of it as the hydrofabric's vector resolution: whole polygons are the smallest pieces we can select. Smaller sub-basins allow finer distinctions between outlets; there is no single fixed size when the polygons have different areas. Some datasets also offer several levels of subdivision. The USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset, for example, organizes hydrologic units into a nested hierarchy identified by Hydrologic Unit Codes (HUCs).

When the hydrofabric provides flow-direction and flow-accumulation rasters, refine can resolve contributing land cell by cell instead. Pourpoint reads the rasters over the whole vector footprint \(M\) and masks out cells outside it. The light-gray grid in the right panel represents this working area. A cell belongs to the mask when its centre falls within \(M\); we denote this set of cells by \(\mathcal G_M\).

docs.title: Choose the outlet cell
docs.text:
The flow-accumulation raster records the upstream contribution to each cell, in the dataset's declared units, such as a cell count or drainage area. Pourpoint examines a small window around \(p\). Among cells inside the mask with valid accumulation and direction values, it selects the one with the greatest accumulation. We call this the outlet cell, \(c_o\).

The default search window is \(3 \times 3\) cells. This is an engineering choice for a local adjustment, with the expectation that users will usually snap their point to the river network first. It is configurable, not a universal optimum: a larger window can select a different branch near a junction. See refinement conventions.

docs.title: Trace upstream cells
docs.text:
The flow-direction raster records which neighbouring cell receives each cell's flow. Pourpoint currently supports the D8 model, in which that neighbour is one of the eight surrounding cells. Datasets can encode those eight directions with different numbers; Pourpoint supports ESRI, TauDEM and unsigned or signed GRASS encodings. See raster encodings.

Let \(d(c)\) denote the downstream cell receiving flow from cell \(c\), when its direction defines one. For example, \(d(a)=b\) means that cell \(a\) drains directly into cell \(b\). To find cells upstream of \(b\), we look for neighbours whose downstream destination is \(b\).

Starting with the outlet, we build successive upstream sets:

\[ C_0 = \{c_o\}, \qquad C_{k+1} = \{c \in \mathcal G_M \mid d(c) \in C_k\}. \]

The next set contains cells inside the mask that drain directly into a cell in the current set. Thus \(C_1\) contains cells one flow step upstream of the outlet, \(C_2\) contains cells two steps upstream, and so on. Cells with no defined downstream neighbour do not satisfy this condition.

Combining these sets gives all contributing cells, including the outlet:

\[ \mathcal C = \bigcup_{k=0}^{\infty} C_k. \]

The infinity symbol expresses “all upstream steps.” In execution, Pourpoint does not revisit cells it has already found and stops when no new cells remain. Accumulation is used to select the outlet; direction determines the upstream connections. An upstream cell can therefore contribute even if its accumulation value is missing.

docs.title: Construct the refined footprint
docs.text:
Let \(\operatorname{footprint}(c)\) be the polygon occupied by raster cell \(c\). We combine these cell footprints and clip them to the vector footprint:

\[ W_{\mathrm{refined}}(p) = M \cap \bigcup_{c \in \mathcal C} \operatorname{footprint}(c). \]

The intersection with \(M\) clips boundary cells to the original vector footprint. In the right panel, the pale-purple refined area includes land draining through \(u_1\) and part of the terminal unit, but excludes the right-hand branch through \(u_2\).

Refinement assumes vector–raster consistency

In the two-panel figure, \(q\) is the terminal unit's declared outlet: the place where drainage leaves that sub-basin. It is different from our requested outlet \(p\), which can lie farther upstream within the unit.

Let \(W_R(q)\) be the watershed obtained from the flow-direction raster at the cell corresponding to \(q\). Masking refinement to \(M\) assumes

\[ M \equiv W_R(q). \]

We mean equivalent drainage coverage at raster resolution, not identical pixel and vector boundaries. Refining at the declared outlet \(q\) should recover the drainage area represented by the vector footprint.

If the selected outlet's raster drainage reaches \(q\), its contributing area is contained in that larger watershed:

\[ W_R(p) \subseteq W_R(q) \equiv M. \]

This is the assumption that makes restricting the trace to \(M\) safe. It has not yet been tested on the available datasets with rasters. Successful refinement does not verify it: a masked trace cannot discover contributing land outside the mask. How to check or declare consistency remains open; issue #180 records the deferred checking utility.

docs.title: Generalizing from a point to a region
docs.text:
Instead of asking which land drains to one point, we can ask which land drains to any point in a target geometry: a lake, a river reach, or a region. We call this its upstream contributing area. Think of it as the hydrological extent of the target—the land that contributes drainage to it.

Let \(R\) be the target geometry, and let \(W(p)\) denote the watershed of a point \(p\). Then

\[ U(R) = \bigcup_{p \in R} W(p). \]

Here \(p\) ranges over every spatial point belonging to \(R\), including its interior and boundary. Imagine placing an outlet at each of those points and combining their watersheds. That combined area is \(U(R)\). Land within the target is included: it already reaches the target without travelling downstream.

A point watershed is the single-point case:

\[ U(\{p\}) = W(p). \]

docs.title: Vector delineation of a region
docs.text:
For a regional target, we select every sub-basin whose polygon shares any part of \(R\). This includes polygons wholly inside the region, polygons crossing its boundary, and polygons touching its boundary. We call this set of terminal units \(T_R\):

\[ T_R = \{b \mid P_b \cap R \neq \varnothing\}. \]

The condition means that the polygon and the region have a nonempty intersection; it does not require their boundaries to cross.

For each terminal unit \(t\), we collect \(\mathcal B_t\), including \(t\) itself. We then combine the selected sets and their polygons:

\[ \mathcal B_R = \bigcup_{t \in T_R} \mathcal B_t, \qquad M_R = \bigcup_{b \in \mathcal B_R} P_b. \]

Every unit in \(T_R\) therefore remains in the result, alongside its upstream contributors. \(U(R)\) is the conceptual contributing area, while \(M_R\) is its representation using whole sub-basin polygons. Pourpoint currently uses this vector representation for regions; raster refinement is available for point outlets.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Python 3.13 or newer and uv. From an authorized checkout of the private Pourpoint repository, run:

uv sync

Run Python through uv run python in that checkout. No PyPI release is required. For another Python project, install the checkout as a local dependency with uv add /path/to/pourpoint.

docs.title: Choose an HFX bundle
docs.text:
Supply HydroFabric with a local bundle directory or an accessible HTTP(S) or S3 bundle location. Its root manifest must select all three current representation values: format_version: "0.4.0", representation: "spatial-geoparquet-adjacency" and representation_version: 1. The format version alone is not sufficient. See bundle discovery. Source normalization belongs to HFX, not Pourpoint.

Vector operations need catchment or river features and the applicable supplied relationships. Point refinement also needs a declared, covering direction and accumulation raster pair. Vector-only bundles remain valid; unavailable rasters are not silently replaced with coarse results.

docs.title: Source lifetime and coordinates
docs.text:
Use HydroFabric as a context manager. Finish source-dependent operations and exports inside the context. Calls are eager; materialized vector results survive closure. A fabric instance is not a concurrent-query service.

Vector targets use WGS84 longitude/latitude, in that order. Native raster outputs retain their own CRS and affine transform. Snapping radius is in metres; the refinement window is measured in native cells.

The optional cache_dir selects a persistent byte-range cache. With the default cache enabled, the first manifest snapshot is retained. Use a new cache directory to adopt another publication deliberately. offline=True replays acquired ranges; a partial cache cannot answer requests for data it never acquired.

See runtime access for cache, transport and identity guarantees and operations for selection and failure semantics. The generated core API documents supported calls and returned values.

docs.title: Data terms
docs.text: The MIT code license does not replace source-data licenses. Preserve each bundle's attribution and provenance in derived outputs. GRIT data carry CC BY-NC 4.0 terms and source caveats.

docs.title: Hydrological operations
docs.text: All vector targets and source features use WGS84 longitude/latitude. Operations are eager; use HydroFabric as a context manager. HFX supplies source identities, attributes, relationships and provenance; clipped pieces do not recompute source areas or orders.

docs.title: Selection and refinement conventions
docs.text:
Selection defaults to catchment level 1, never the finest available level. Point boundary ownership uses the smallest intersecting source ID. Regions include boundary intersections. Empty geometries give valid empty selections; nonempty targets with no intersecting unit raise selection.no_coverage. Missing or explicitly unsupplied connectivity fails rather than returning an apparently complete answer. Malformed flow edges crossing levels raise an integrity error.

Refinement assumes vector/raster equivalence; it does not certify that scientific assumption. The whole selected vector footprint is the computational mask. Native cells are admitted by their centers using GDAL rasterization. The local window defaults to 3 by 3 cells, with positive odd sizes accepted. Outlet choice requires valid direction and accumulation, maximizes accumulation, and breaks ties in source row/column order. Reverse tracing uses direction validity alone: an upstream cell with missing accumulation can still contribute. Zero and negative signed directions terminate flow. No direction pointers are warped.

Polygonized cells are clipped to the original combined vector footprint, then intersected with source polygons for granular output. This keeps merged granular and footprint outputs equivalent, without hole filling or untouched upstream units. The outlet cell retains global source-grid row/column, CRS and affine. Its center is a display location, not improved station accuracy.

docs.title: Batches and failures
docs.text:
Dictionary keys name targets; list entries receive UUIDs once per accepted batch. Duplicate geometries remain independent targets. BatchResult.targets preserves names, original geometries and input indices alongside ordered result slots. Expected failures have a None slot and a durable BatchIssue. Configuration, integrity and unexpected programming failures raise instead of becoming issues. Single-target OperationError exposes the same code and reason.

n_jobs=1 executes sequentially. Positive bounds and -1 (available CPUs) use bounded threads with one independent fabric context per worker chunk. Contexts are reused across that chunk, never shared between worker threads. They use the same persistent cache and verify the same manifest snapshot. Parent fabric.stats includes worker requests, received payload bytes and cache-hit bytes. Concurrent first requests may duplicate acquisitions; this is not a single-flight cache. The number of simultaneous results and raster arrays grows with worker count.

Explicit batch selection can feed refine(fabric=fabric, subbasins=selection) without regenerating identity. Existing failures remain failures.

docs.title: Rivers and snapping
docs.text:
River level defaults independently to 1. select_rivers clips to the combined footprint, not each constituent unit. include_downstream=True follows supplied directed edges through splits and reconvergence. For a boundary inside a feature, its downstream suffix is retained. Source orientation or exactly matching supplied endpoint-node coordinates establish direction; ambiguous geometry raises rivers.ambiguous_direction rather than inventing flow. Source features, attributes, relationships and nodes survive clipping. Their endpoints are not reclassified as natural outlets.

snap minimizes WGS84 ground distance to supplied straight longitude/latitude stream segments. It uses 64 golden-section iterations per segment, plus endpoints and exact on-segment checks; this is a local stream-segment numerical method, not a global optimizer for globe-spanning linework. Split antimeridian crossings before calling. Radius is metres and delineate defaults it to 100 when snapping is requested. Snapping and raster outlet adjustment are separate operations.

docs.title: Portable output
docs.text:
QGISBundle writes a new folder containing watershed.qgz, vectors.gpkg and GeoTIFFs. It refuses to overwrite an existing folder. Project references are relative; move the whole folder together. Raw vector geometries require an explicit crs=. add_result includes available outputs only, with per-target groups and issues. It does not merge or trace rivers implicitly.

Each refined target receives one native-grid direction/accumulation pair, masked to the whole vector delineation. Direction values retain their source encoding, not the normalized codes used internally for tracing. Values outside the mask or invalid in the corresponding band become source nodata. The outlet outline is in the raster CRS. Raster descriptors currently hold eager caller-owned arrays, so export adds no source fetches; export inside the fabric context remains the supported workflow. Memory includes these arrays for every retained refinement result.

GeoPackage features expose ordinary scalar attributes. Rich values, exact Arrow types/nulls and field/schema metadata remain lossless Arrow IPC stream blobs in source_arrow, keyed by layer and source row or relationship kind. Use pyarrow.ipc.open_stream(payload).read_all() to read them. source_metadata keeps attribute-column mappings and source declarations; colliding scalar names receive source_ prefixes. river_connections exposes directed supplied relations as ordinary rows, alongside lossless relationship and node tables. Target identity columns are separate from source IDs. Original source geometry remains in Arrow provenance even where a displayed feature is clipped.

Exports retain GRIT's CC BY-NC 4.0 terms, attribution and source caveats. The code license does not grant different rights to data or exported results.

docs.title: Native-grid raster access
docs.text:
The HFX 0.4.0 raster contract optionally declares hfx.aux.d8_raster.v2 pairs in the root manifest. The retained source manifest is provenance, not a discovery channel. Vector-only bundles remain valid. Raster headers are not opened for vector use. External artifact references resolve their declared HTTPS URL, fingerprint and retention commitment; the raster pair need not be stored beside the vectors.

Bounds default to EPSG:4326. Pass crs="EPSG:8857" for bounds already on that native CRS. Bounds use the supplied CRS's coordinate units, including geographic CRSs expressed in grads rather than degrees. Requests have positive area and must use a nonwrapping envelope (no antimeridian wrap). Preparation transforms all four envelope edges with 101 interior samples per edge, not just two opposite corners. It uses the declared CRS of each pair, then encloses the transformed envelope in whole native cells. This is conservative edge sampling, not exact symbolic projection of arbitrary curved edges. Supplying native bounds avoids that approximation. The direction raster is never warped. A pair must cover the entire request. There is no mosaicking or overlap arbitration; any fully covering coherent pair can be selected.

First preparation opens and validates pair headers. Once open, preparation uses only grid metadata, with no pixel reads. Reader-bound frozen requests carry grid CRS, affine, dimensions and both published SHA-256 identities. Requests from another reader are rejected. The reader reuses ordinary synchronous GDAL handles. There is no batch, scheduling or async API.

docs.title: Results and semantics
docs.text:
RasterWindow contains caller-owned arrays, transform, crs and accumulation_units, and the original native-grid .request descriptor. Results survive later reads, mutations of later results and reader closure. The descriptor records the exact grid/window for future raster export without reconstructing it.

  • direction is int8: 1 E, 2 SE, 3 S, 4 SW, 5 W, 6 NW, 7 N, 8 NE. These are native grid neighbors: E increases column and S increases row, even for a rotated affine.
  • Zero is a terminal cell. Negative directions preserve signed GRASS exiting-flow meaning; they are terminal for upstream tracing, but retain the exit direction.
  • direction_valid and accumulation_valid are separate boolean masks. A false direction mask has a zero payload, not a valid terminal cell. Header nodata takes precedence over codes. Invalid consumed data raises an error.
  • accumulation retains native int32 or float32 values and bits. It is never converted through float32 from int32. Units are cells or km2 exactly as declared. GRIT's width-partitioned drainage area remains width-partitioned km²; the reader does not convert it into another area definition.

The reader supports ESRI, TauDEM and unsigned/signed GRASS direction encodings. It checks consumed declarations, fingerprints, pair CRS/grid, band count, dtype/nodata and consumed values. It trusts producer conformance for internal layout, overlap coherence, coverage union and hydrology. Native-only tiled TIFFs without overviews are supported. Opening does not hash whole rasters or read whole tile indexes.

Missing declarations raise MissingRastersError. No covering pair raises RasterCoverageError. Invalid declarations, headers or consumed values raise ValueError; unreadable raster data raises Rasterio/GDAL read errors. These failures do not choose a coarse-watershed fallback.

docs.title: Lifetime and transport
docs.text:
Direct RasterReader access avoids catchment metadata acquisition. Close the reader before its Source during direct access. Create and use each reader on one thread. One reader allows one active call. Future concurrent workers must create private Sources and reader pairs in their own threads, not share ordinary GDAL handles. Closing releases handles, not every process-wide GDAL cache. GDAL owns block-cache budgeting and any process-wide VSICURL state; Pourpoint adds no worker pool, separate raster cache or service-wide memory budget. Original TIFF ranges share the accumulating persistent cache described in runtime access.

Rasterio uses a Python opener with independent fsspec cursors over the existing Source's pinned obstore range access. It does not independently open the remote URL with GDAL, copy credentials into GDAL settings, or pass a file object to Rasterio's eager MemoryFile path. Local, HTTP and S3-compatible configuration therefore use the same Source guarantees as vectors. Controlled S3 fixtures test signed configured-endpoint access; public GRIT is HTTP evidence, not a live credentialed S3 deployment test.

Source requests send Cache-Control: no-cache to revalidate publication responses. With persistent caching, the first manifest snapshot also survives reopening. offline=True replays acquired TIFF ranges without contacting the origin. An old vector-only snapshot is not supplemented by discovering undeclared files. Raster opening checks size and bounded head/tail hashes. Every new remote range uses the original strong ETag/version and validates the response. Cached bytes remain part of that original snapshot; cached reads do not probe whether the latest remote object changed. Local identities are checked before/after calls, even on cached reads. Bounded checks are not whole-file integrity proofs.

HydroFabric.buffer_bytes includes fsspec cursor buffers, not GDAL native caches or caller-owned result arrays. Array bytes and process RSS are different quantities. Rasterio 1.5.2's Python read callback does not safely propagate arbitrary Python transport exceptions through native frames. A raster-only cursor records the first transport error and signals a short read to GDAL; immediately after the native operation, the reader raises the original Python error. No partial window is returned. Error state is scoped to the operation; a later read of already cached coherent data remains usable. Tests cover missing cached header/pixel bytes and changed remote identity, including a subsequent healthy reader. Ordinary file reads clip at EOF; the underlying exact-range transport still rejects invalid ranges.

GRIT data retain their bundle's CC BY-NC 4.0 license, attribution, provenance and source caveats. Pourpoint's code license does not replace those terms.

docs.title: Runtime access
docs.text:
HydroFabric reads the final HFX 0.4.0 spatial-geoparquet-adjacency representation (version 1), including catchments, rivers, source nodes and native rasters. Opening reads only the manifest, not worldwide indexes or feature tables.

These are source-reader operations. See hydrological operations for upstream selection, delineation, refinement, snapping and portable export.

docs.title: Selected records and relationships
docs.text:
• records(domain, ids, columns=None) returns a materialized Arrow table. Domains are catchments, rivers, and river_nodes. Input order and duplicates survive; any missing ID raises KeyError. Projection avoids acquiring/decompressing unwanted Parquet columns where the format permits.
  • candidates(domain, bounds, levels=None, columns=None) selects conservative bbox overlaps in physical file order. Bounds are WGS84 west/south/east/north. Parquet statistics prune groups; missing statistics retain them. Record bounds and tiers refine candidates before full records are read using their discovered addresses. Bbox overlap is not exact geometry intersection or point containment.
  • relationships(domain, ids, columns=None) returns all supplied immediate relationship columns unless projected. manifest.relationships retains source meanings, direction, target domain and artifact bindings. Flow, hierarchy, incidence, cross-tier node correspondence and drainage association remain distinct.
  • traverse(domain, ids, relationship="upstream_ids") returns an inclusive, breadth-first same-domain closure, deduplicating splits/reconvergence and cycles. Missing/not-supplied connectivity and empty lists never classify natural outlets. Traversal keeps an estimated 8 MiB adjacency reuse cache; per-call visited state and returned IDs necessarily scale with the selected closure, not the world.

subbasins(ids) and nodes(ids) return ordinary lists of Arrow-backed features. river_network(ids) retains selected river features, complete selected-row relationships and supplied endpoint nodes with their relationships. Its .geometry exposes linework; it does not replace individual features. boundary_river_ids identifies supplied flow neighbors omitted from the selected rivers. They remain references, not invented terminals or connections.

Each feature exposes .id, .geometry, .wkb and .attributes. WKB remains exact source bytes; decoding geometry is explicit property access and does not rewrite source values. attributes["source_strahler_order"] returns the supplied typed Python value or None; no stream order is inferred. attributes.scalar(name) and attributes.schema expose original Arrow types, field/schema metadata and rich values without lossy coercion. Full .table retains all fields, including WKB. Source provenance remains discoverable in fabric.manifest.declarations.

docs.title: Lifetime and persistent cache
docs.text:
Use one context manager per sequential workload. Calls are eager; combine IDs to share lookup, relationship and feature reads. Instances are not a concurrent-query service. Materialized tables and features survive closure. Source-dependent raster reads must finish inside the context. Closing releases readers/connections and leaves persistent cache content intact.

Caching defaults to cache=True. cache_dir selects the location; otherwise it is ~/Library/Caches/pourpoint on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA%/pourpoint on Windows, and $XDG_CACHE_HOME/pourpoint (or ~/.cache/pourpoint) elsewhere. cache=False disables disk caching, not bounded in-memory buffering.

One SQLite cache accumulates original byte ranges by source, artifact fingerprint and address. Atomic writes retain only acquired coverage and deduplicate overlap. No private feature format, index rebuild, per-watershed bundle or automatic disk eviction is involved. Cached manifest bytes pin the first snapshot in that cache. To deliberately adopt a newer publication, choose a new cache directory or remove the old cache when no readers are using it.

offline=True prohibits network acquisition, including HEAD. Completed workloads can replay with their cache intact. Missing metadata or payload raises a clear error, never partial results or a different snapshot. A partial cache is not a standalone complete HFX bundle. Users control cache retention. Cache metadata is trusted local state, not a tamper-proof database; stored range checksums detect accidental payload corruption.

docs.title: Rasters, transport and measurement
docs.text:
fabric.rasters resolves the manifest's local or external direction/accumulation pair lazily. See native-grid raster access. Requests carry native grid and window descriptors for future export; no direction-pointer warping occurs. Missing rasters or inadequate coverage are errors.

Local paths, anonymous HTTP(S) and S3 use the shared checked obstore transport; storage_options passes its constructor options. URLs must not carry credentials. External raster URLs on another origin use anonymous transport; credentials and source-specific configuration are never forwarded across origins. Remote range reads pin a strong ETag or immutable version and check range, encoding, identity and length. Lookup metadata binds addresses to the exact feature digest; relationship declarations bind every involved domain. Directories are fully hashed; feature/IPC/TIFF bounded head/tail fingerprints are selective checks, not full artifact verification. Immutable producer publication remains required.

Cached Parquet reads prefetch projected column chunks with four concurrent checked transfers, split at 8 MiB each, without coalescing gaps. Scheduling is per row group, not worldwide. These are initial engineering constants, not proven optima or a 32 MiB RSS guarantee: SQLite copies, decoding and returned data have separate memory costs. The existing obstore transport was retained after examining fsspec async scheduling, avoiding a second authentication/integrity path.

stats reports source requests (including HEAD), response payload bytes and disk cache-hit bytes, shared with external rasters. It is not wire traffic. buffer_bytes reports retained serialized source buffers, spatial statistics arrays and estimated adjacency storage, not process RSS, Arrow/GDAL metadata, query results or geometry allocations. Spatial arrays are prepared on the first candidate query per domain and retain 50 bytes per Parquet row group; ID-only reads do not prepare them.

docs.title: HFX
docs.text:
HydroFabric Exchange (HFX) is a format for sharing hydrofabric data.

In HFX, we understand a hydrofabric as a dataset that tiles the landscape into sub-basins, describes their downstream connections and provides the river network alongside auxiliary data, when available, such as the flow-direction and flow-accumulation rasters used to produce it.

The map below shows the GRIT hydrofabric over Switzerland. Each grey polygon is a sub-basin, with the supplied rivers shown in blue. The dataset is clipped to Switzerland for display.

Boundaries: Natural Earth. Their depiction implies no position on territorial status.

HFX brings these pieces together in a bundle with a common structure. It preserves source identities, attributes, connections and provenance, and describes where each part of the dataset can be found. This lets tools such as Pourpoint read prepared hydrofabrics through one interface to select rivers and delineate watersheds.

The documentation explains the data model, bundle organization, vector storage and optional native-grid rasters. This repository contains the specification and supporting tools for preparing and verifying bundles.

docs.title: Bundle organization and discovery
docs.text:
A bundle contains one UTF-8 manifest.json and the artifacts it identifies. Read the root manifest rather than guessing filenames or consulting a source manifest for runtime addresses. Select the current representation using all three values:

{
  "format_version": "0.4.0",
  "representation": "spatial-geoparquet-adjacency",
  "representation_version": 1
}

The format string alone does not establish compatibility with earlier IPC feature publications. Current features use GeoParquet; lookup and immediate relationship files use Arrow IPC. The manifest discovers each independently.

Local paths are relative POSIX paths within the bundle root and must not escape it. Only explicit external raster references may name remote objects. Each local path names one immutable data or provenance file. Readers accept additional manifest fields and validate fields they use.

docs.title: Manifest fields
docs.text:
Field Meaning format_version, representation, representation_version Exact selector above fabric_name Lowercase ASCII source-fabric name fabric_version Optional source-fabric version string crs "EPSG:4326" for vectors; raster CRS is declared separately has_up_area Boolean; computed upstream areas available when true, with per-row nulls permitted; all null when false topology "tree" or "dag" for supplied same-level catchment connectivity bbox Four finite numbers [west, south, east, north] covering the units unit_count Positive catchment count created_at, adapter_version Source normalization RFC 3339 timestamp and adapter version region Optional source subset string families Feature domain declarations, below relationships Immediate relationship declarations, below catchment_connectivity One { "level": integer, "status": "supplied" or "not_supplied" } per catchment level categorical_columns Optional typed column dictionaries auxiliary Array of optional D8 pairs; may be empty external_artifacts Optional external raster identities artifacts Fingerprints of every local delivered artifact except the root manifest source_manifest Path source-manifest.json to preserved normalized input bytes addressing block: zero-based Parquet row group; row: zero-based row within group input_manifest_sha256 Full SHA-256 binding the preserved source-manifest.json bytes source_domain_metadata Preserved nonphysical river/node declarations, including supplied river topology

families maps represented catchments, rivers, and river_nodes to separate ID domains. Each declaration supplies data, data_sha256, count, lookup, and directory. Counts are exact positive feature and lookup row counts. Omit unsupplied optional domains, including associated feature, lookup and relationship declarations; empty feature files are not an alternative. Nodes require rivers.

relationships maps represented domains to IPC data, ID-range directory, columns provenance and feature_artifacts bindings. Optional relationship columns are discovered from these declarations; absent evidence is not an empty supplied relationship. See storage and access.

docs.title: Provenance and attribution
docs.text: Preserve source identities, typed attributes, metadata, normalization provenance, original inventory, licensing and attribution. source-manifest.json retains exact verified normalized input bytes; it is provenance, not current feature addressing. NOTICE, CITATION.txt and dataset publication notes carry applicable licenses, transformations and caveats. GRIT data remains CC BY-NC 4.0, separate from this repository's MIT code license. A new physical layout does not certify source hydrology. Source and derived quantities retain their distinct meanings.

docs.title: Artifact identity and range access
docs.text:
Each fingerprint has nonnegative integer size_bytes and lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 strings sha256, head_sha256, tail_sha256. The first is the whole-file digest. The latter two hash the first and last min(65536, size_bytes) bytes. Consumers check sizes and bounded hashes before using lookup and feature artifacts, verify the lookup's hfx:data_sha256 binding, and verify the directory's full digest. Bounded hashes detect mismatches within their checked regions. Complete integrity uses full producer and upload verification, a trusted manifest and immutable data artifacts. Consumers needing independent integrity assurance verify full digests.

Locate IPC batches through the file trailer: a little-endian 32-bit footer length followed by the six bytes ARROW1. The footer supplies record-batch offsets and lengths. Fetch schema and dictionary dependencies required by Arrow. The lookup uses plain numeric arrays. Read the directory and IPC footer metadata at startup; fetch numeric lookup batches only for requested IDs. Feature addresses refer to Parquet row groups, whose boundaries come from Parquet metadata, not the IPC footer.

HTTP servers return 206 Partial Content for requested byte ranges over the stored bytes. Clients send Accept-Encoding: identity, verify Content-Range and response length, and pin a strong ETag or immutable object version across requests. ETags identify transport versions; the manifest supplies full SHA-256 identity. Reject changed identities, malformed ranges, out-of-bounds addresses and mismatched fingerprints. Reading one bundle requires a consistent manifest and artifact object set for the duration of access.

For a new bundle, publish verified artifacts at an unused versioned prefix, verify uploaded identities, then publish the manifest. Keep data artifacts immutable. Corrections to data artifacts use a new prefix and manifest with fresh bindings.

docs.title: External raster artifacts
docs.text:
Only raster auxiliaries may refer outside the bundle. In a raster declaration, replace a local artifact path with {"external": "raster-flow-dir"} (or another unique key). That key resolves in root external_artifacts to an object with url, size_bytes, sha256, head_sha256, tail_sha256, and retention. url is a direct absolute HTTPS data-object URL, not another manifest or a mutable alias. Fingerprints have exactly the local artifact meanings. retention is a nonempty concrete publisher commitment identifying who keeps that exact object immutable and publicly available for the lifetime of this dependent bundle; it is not an automatic runtime guarantee. External keys are not local artifact paths and do not appear in artifacts.

Publishers verify the referenced full identity and provenance, retain the original verification receipt, and check current public range reads before publishing a new manifest. References may reuse unchanged verified objects without copying or reprocessing them. All size, range, encoding, fingerprint and pinned strong ETag/object-version checks still apply. Access retains one consistent root manifest snapshot, including its external identities; it must not refresh another bundle's manifest to resolve a reference. A missing or changed object is an error, not permission to substitute data. Document this cross-prefix lifetime dependency. Preserve existing publications and their valid manifest snapshots.

docs.title: Features and identity
docs.text:
A catchment is a drainage polygon at a declared resolution tier. A river is a source river feature, not a catchment boundary or a universal snapping segment. Optional source nodes describe river endpoints. Nodes are not invented where the source supplies none. Catchments, rivers and nodes have independent positive integer ID domains: the same number in two domains identifies different objects. IDs are dataset-local, not row positions or globally stable identifiers.

Source identity is separate. source_namespace and source_id retain the source layer and feature identity; native identifier fields retain their own types. Coincident geometry or a shared association key does not merge source features.

docs.title: Relationships answer different questions
docs.text:
• Hierarchy: parent and child relations connect coarser and finer tiers. Smaller level numbers are coarser. River and catchment tiers are independent.
  • Flow: upstream and downstream relations describe supplied same-tier directed connectivity. They are immediate edges, not precomputed contributing basins.
  • Node incidence: endpoints connect rivers to source nodes. Sharing a node does not supply every possible incoming-to-outgoing flow edge.
  • Node correspondence: coarser and finer nodes preserve source cross-tier correspondence, not polygon containment or river constituent membership.
  • Drainage associations: local catchments describe local drainage associated with a river. Component catchments describe a connected network component. Neither is automatically the accumulated upstream contributing area.

A river can have multiple represented local catchments. The authoritative local_catchment_ids lists and reverse local_river_ids preserve all associations. Do not infer associations solely from spatial intersection.

docs.title: Missing information is not a terminal
docs.text: An empty adjacency list is valid but does not alone say that a feature is a natural outlet. catchment_connectivity distinguishes supplied connectivity from a level with no supplied edges. Feature nulls and source coverage metadata separate no represented association from unavailable evidence. Subset cuts retain external source edge identities and caveats; they do not become source terminals. Optional absent domains are not dummy empty feature tables.

docs.title: Quantities and geometry
docs.text:
area_km2 is local geodesic polygon area. up_area_km2 is inclusive same-level upstream area under documented dataset semantics. Native source area, partitioned drainage area, mainstem-following area and polygon-union area are not interchangeable. Unsupported upstream values remain null. A single outlet coordinate is supplied only when the source describes one outlet; multiple or absent outlets are not replaced by an arbitrary point.

Vector coordinates use longitude/latitude WGS84. Geometry retains its source meaning and normalized WKB; packaging does not repair flow continuity. Optional D8 rasters retain their native grids and declared encoding and units. Raster accumulation and vector upstream area can describe different quantities.

docs.title: HFX 0.4.0 Raster Data
docs.text: This optional auxiliary contract extends the bundle with a native-grid D8 direction and accumulation pair. HFX 0.4.0 explicitly supports native-only, internally tiled, cloud-friendly TIFF layout without overviews. This is not a claim of strict overview-bearing COG conformance. Successful packaging does not certify hydrological equivalence or source hydrology.

docs.title: Manifest declaration
docs.text:
Each pair is an entry in the root manifest's auxiliary array, alongside any other auxiliaries. Both artifact references are required. A local path is relative to the bundle root and must not escape it; its file has an entry in the root artifacts fingerprint map. Alternatively, { "external": "key" } resolves to the root external_artifacts identity under the external raster rules. Do not place URLs or ../ escapes in local-path strings. Both forms require size, full SHA-256 and head/tail SHA-256 as defined by the bundle identity rules. A retained source manifest is provenance, not a raster declaration.

A pair declaration has this structure (CRS, encoding and units describe that pair):

{
  "schema": "hfx.aux.d8_raster.v2",
  "artifacts": {
    "flow_dir": "aux/d8/flow_dir.tif",
    "flow_acc": "aux/d8/flow_acc.tif"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "crs": "EPSG:8857",
    "flow_dir_encoding": "grass",
    "flow_acc_units": "km2"
  }
}

The three metadata fields are required, without defaults or additional metadata properties. crs is an uppercase EPSG authority string matching ^EPSG:[1-9][0-9]*$. flow_dir_encoding is esri, taudem or grass. flow_acc_units is cells or km2. The manifest's existing top-level crs remains the vector CRS (EPSG:4326); it does not override a raster entry's CRS.

docs.title: Native grid and headers
docs.text:
GeoTIFF headers are authoritative for dtype and nodata. Each raster must carry a nodata tag; its value is not constrained by this contract. Do not duplicate dtype or nodata in declaration metadata. Direction dtype is uint8 or int8. Accumulation dtype is float32 for cells (upstream cell count), or int32 or float32 for km2 (upstream drainage area in square kilometers).

Both header CRSs must resolve to the declared CRS. A pair must share CRS, dimensions, affine transform, pixel dimensions and grid alignment. Keep direction on the grid where its neighbor pointers were derived: neither producers nor consumers may warp it to another CRS. There is no universal raster CRS, numeric representation or compression recipe.

Both files must be readable, internally tiled GeoTIFFs arranged for bounded HTTP range reads. Use BigTIFF when offsets exceed classic TIFF limits. Native-only layout is supported: overviews are not required. Record expected validator warnings about missing recommended overviews separately; do not suppress other layout or validation failures. Verify offsets, tile ranges and actual range reads rather than inferring suitability from a file extension.

docs.title: Direction meaning
docs.text:
The declared encoding selects one column:

Direction ESRI TauDEM GRASS East 1 1 8 Southeast 2 8 7 South 4 7 6 Southwest 8 6 5 West 16 5 4 Northwest 32 4 3 North 64 3 2 Northeast 128 2 1

ESRI uses powers of two. TauDEM numbers counterclockwise from east; GRASS r.watershed numbers counterclockwise from northeast. For GRASS with uint8, valid data codes are 0 through 8; 0 denotes a terminal cell with no downstream neighbor. For signed GRASS values, a negative value gives the direction of its absolute value and indicates flow exiting raster coverage. Negative values and 0 (sink or depression) are terminal for upstream tracing. Nodata is determined by the header, not by guessing from the direction codes. Engines normalize the declared encoding on read; this contract does not implement refinement.

docs.title: Coverage and overlap
docs.text:
Each entry declares its own CRS; entries may use different EPSG CRSs. Geographically overlapping entries must be windows of the same grid: same CRS, pixel dimensions, pixel basis and alignment. Every shared cell must have identical direction and accumulation values in all overlapping entries. Entries on different grids must have disjoint geographic footprints. A consumer may use any entry covering the whole requested region; it need not mosaic or arbitrate between coherent overlaps.

For each raster, transform the extent to EPSG:4326 with densified edge sampling and check intersection with the manifest bbox. Sampling density is an implementation choice. This is a gross-mislocation smoke check, not proof of precise coverage. The union of entries should cover the manifest bbox. Consumers may query coverage from headers at read time.

docs.title: Discovery and identity
docs.text:
manifest.json has format_version: "0.4.0", representation: "spatial-geoparquet-adjacency", and representation_version: 1. families maps represented catchments, rivers, and river_nodes to independent ID domains. Omit unsupplied domains such as source nodes, including their feature, lookup and relationship declarations; do not create dummy files or invent nodes. Each declaration supplies data, data_sha256, count, lookup and directory. artifacts gives full SHA-256, size and bounded head/tail fingerprints of every local data, index and provenance artifact. Paths are bundle-relative. Full hashes are production identities; bounded fingerprints are selective-access checks, not proof that all bytes were verified. A manifest is published only after its files.

One GeoParquet file per domain is authoritative. Fields retain normalized Arrow types, nulls, field/schema metadata, source identities, tiers and exact normalized WKB. Native widths may change only under documented approved lossless source mappings with original per-source declarations retained; TDX catchment streamID uses int64. Only GeoParquet geo metadata is added. Coordinates are longitude/latitude WGS84 (GeoParquet's default CRS84). Attributes can be projected without geometry. Current production orders by tier, 16-bit Morton key and ID. Row groups target 8192 rows and 8 MiB logical bytes, with oversized single rows allowed. These are reversible producer settings, not reader requirements or memory/latency limits. Readers must discover actual group boundaries from Parquet metadata.

docs.title: ID and spatial access
docs.text:
The uncompressed Arrow IPC lookup has nonnull id: int64, block: int32, row: int32, sorted by unique positive ID. block is the zero-based Parquet row group; row is its zero-based row position. Schema metadata hfx:data_sha256 binds addresses to the final Parquet bytes. The lookup directory's batches list contains batch, min_id, max_id, and rows; bounds select candidate lookup batches, not proof that an ID exists. Compare the actual ID before returning a row. Addresses cannot be reused for another physical artifact, even with the same IDs. The lookup fields occur in exactly that order. Schema metadata hfx:data_sha256 contains the ASCII lowercase full feature digest. Lookup batches contain 65536 rows except the final remainder. The UTF-8 JSON directory has version: 1 and exactly one entry per batch in batch order. Inclusive min_id and max_id are its first and last IDs; ranges are disjoint and ascending. Integer parsing must preserve signed 64-bit precision. Every feature appears exactly once, every address is within bounds, and each addressed row contains its stated ID. Binary-search the ranges and then the selected lookup batch for an exact ID; no match means absent. Group matched addresses by Parquet row group to avoid duplicate reads.

Native Parquet statistics on bbox.xmin, bbox.ymin, bbox.xmax, bbox.ymax conservatively select candidate row groups. Use inclusive comparisons and outward rounding when narrowing precision; missing statistics mean retain the group. Then project per-record bounds and tier to refine candidates before fetching full records. Bounds are not exact geometry intersections. No duplicate feature table or mandatory private cache is part of the bundle.

docs.title: Immediate relationships
docs.text:
relationships maps each domain to an independent IPC data file and ID-range directory. Each row contains nonnull id: int64 plus independently projectable nonnull list<int64> columns with nonnull elements. All IDs in the domain have a row, including empty lists. Rows and each neighbor list are sorted. Relationships are immediate, not closures:

  • upstream_ids / downstream_ids: supplied flow graph and its reverse;
  • parent_ids / child_ids: tier hierarchy;
  • upstream_node_ids / outgoing_river_ids, and downstream_node_ids / incoming_river_ids: directed incidence;
  • coarser_node_ids / finer_node_ids: cross-tier node correspondence;
  • local_catchment_ids / local_river_ids, and component_catchment_ids / component_river_ids: distinct drainage associations.

docs.title: Local drainage associations
docs.text:
For this representation, river local_catchment_ids and its exact reverse, catchment local_river_ids, are authoritative. A river may have zero, one or multiple represented local catchments; preserve every supplied association. Keep feature identity separate from association keys: preserve native fields such as TDX streamID independently, without merging distinct source features that share an association key.

The river feature column local_catchment_id may be omitted. If present, it must equal the sole associated catchment ID, or be null when there is no represented association. It cannot represent multiple associations. If any river has multiple local catchments, omit this scalar column from the domain's feature file rather than choosing one catchment or writing a misleading null. See the feature schemas for the other river fields.

Existing GRIT singleton associations and their consistent scalar feature columns remain valid without changing published files or hashes. The physical relationship lists use the same schema for single and plural associations.

TDX river features additionally carry nonnull string local_catchment_coverage: supplied means the basin's polygon source was available and associations were exhaustively checked; unavailable means the polygon source was missing and local associations are unknown. Both may have empty relationship lists; they are not the same evidence. processing_basin connects each feature to the domain coverage and original declarations in source-metadata.json. The manifest's categorical_columns records the field meanings. This TDX extension does not require rewriting existing GRIT publications. Pourpoint support requires explicit coordination; shared version numbers and support for plural lists alone do not establish reader compatibility.

docs.title: Relationship provenance and access
docs.text: Each columns entry records original source artifact/column, direction and domain meaning. feature_artifacts binds involved domains to final feature paths/hashes. Original graph files are provenance, not runtime feature addresses. Follow the relationship's target_domain, then that domain's ID lookup to fetch records. Shared node incidence does not imply a supplied flow edge. Empty lists do not classify terminals or resolve unknown scalar relationships. Consult authoritative feature nulls, catchment_connectivity and preserved source caveats. Consumers own traversal and query workspace.

docs.title: Source and raster preservation
docs.text:
source-manifest.json retains exact verified normalized input manifest bytes; input_manifest_sha256 pins them. Original inventory, normalization provenance, license and attribution remain discoverable through copied provenance and source artifact identities. Category declarations point to final feature files. source_domain_metadata retains nonphysical river/node declarations such as supplied river topology. GRIT remains CC BY-NC 4.0. Storage conversion does not repair hydrology or renormalize WKB.

auxiliary and external_artifacts are copied unchanged, including raster URLs, identities and retention commitments. Declared local D8 raster files are copied byte-for-byte with unchanged artifact identities; missing files or identities and mismatched bytes are rejected. Verification checks these references independently of the converter's provenance inventory. External rasters are not fetched. Raster conformance, public range and decoded-window verification remain separate duties.

docs.title: Vector feature schemas
docs.text: These schemas apply to the current representation. Physical access is specified in spatial layout.

docs.title: Catchments
docs.text:
The catchment GeoParquet file contains one row per drainage unit. Attributes and WKB occupy the same row. The required fields are:

Field Arrow type Nullable Meaning id int64 No Positive dataset-local unique unit ID level int16 No Nonnegative dataset-local resolution tier parent_id int64 Yes Containing unit at a strictly coarser available level area_km2 float32 No Local geodesic area in km² up_area_km2 float32 Yes Inclusive same-level upstream area in km², under documented dataset semantics outlet_lon float64 Yes Finite EPSG:4326 longitude of a single source-described outlet outlet_lat float64 Yes Finite EPSG:4326 latitude of that outlet bbox struct<xmin: float32!, ymin: float32!, xmax: float32!, ymax: float32!> No Finite ordered, outward-covering EPSG:4326 bounds; ! denotes non-nullable leaves geometry binary No Exact Polygon or MultiPolygon WKB in EPSG:4326

Source identity is retained as source_namespace: string and source_id: string (non-nullable). A namespace identifies the source product and layer, including region/basin where needed for unique source identity. The pair identifies a source feature; preserve native ID columns and types independently of the string rendering. Only unchanged catchment artifacts from the earlier normalized 0.4.0 publication may retain their existing optional source identity fields when documented provenance establishes the mapping. Newly produced catchments require both nonnullable fields.

Smaller levels are coarser. Each coarsest unit has null parent_id; other nonnull parents resolve at a strictly coarser available catchment level. A child polygon must lie within its declared parent, and sibling polygon interiors must not overlap, within explicitly documented numerical geometry tolerances. A producer declares the tolerance values, units and comparison method and reports actual validation coverage. This contract does not require exhaustive worldwide polygon topology certification; full reference and source-fidelity verification is a separate duty. Tolerances account for numerical representation, not arbitrary source discrepancies. A violation beyond them is nonconforming; recording an anomaly does not waive the invariant. Investigate such originals and obtain an explicit contract decision before production rather than silently repairing geometry or relaxing containment. Record validation coverage separately: sampled checks do not establish worldwide conformance. Components may have multiple or no represented outlets, including coastal and inland sink polygon-only units. Outlet coordinates are either both null or both present. Supply them only for a single source-described outlet; never choose an arbitrary representative from multiple outlets or invent a point. Source river nodes and associations retain multiple outlet facts independently.

catchment_connectivity distinguishes supplied edges from absent information. For a not_supplied level, every graph row has an empty upstream list; that is not an assertion of natural termination. The topology declaration applies only to supplied levels. Even there, missing links alone do not classify a terminal. Preserve source explanations and distinguish subset cuts. Additional typed source attributes and nulls remain intact. Preserve native local polygon area separately from geodesic area_km2; partitioned drainage area, mainstem-following area and upstream polygon-union area are different quantities. Do not relabel one as another. Document upstream-area semantics, derivations and anomalies; use null rather than an unsupported value.

docs.title: Rivers
docs.text:
Field Arrow type Nullable Meaning id int64 No Positive dataset-local river ID, unique across river levels level int16 No Nonnegative river tier; smaller is coarser parent_id int64 Yes Constituent membership in a river at a strictly coarser available tier source_namespace, source_id string No Source layer identity and ID rendering; retain native ID separately local_catchment_id (optional column) int64 Yes Sole represented local drainage association; see plural association rules component_catchment_id int64 Yes Associated drainage unit representing the connected network component upstream_node_id, downstream_node_id int64 Yes Source-directed endpoint references to node rows geometry_orientation int8 No 0 unspecified, 1 upstream-first, 2 downstream-first bbox Catchment bbox struct No Outward-covering EPSG:4326 bounds geometry binary No LineString or MultiLineString WKB in EPSG:4326

The local_catchment_id column is optional. The authoritative plural local drainage associations determine whether it may be included and what its values mean.

Within each feature table, (source_namespace, source_id) is unique across all levels; river, node and catchment tables have separate HFX ID domains. Namespaces retain source layer identity, not a label inferred from coincident geometry. River IDs are not row numbers or globally stable IDs across datasets/versions. River and catchment tiers are independent. One-tier rivers need no invented parents. Stream order is an attribute, not a tier or universal snapping weight. Parent membership does not require equality with the union of child geometries. Each nonnull catchment association resolves to a catchment ID; multiple rivers may share either target. Sources need not supply components or polygons. Null means no represented association, with absence versus unavailable evidence documented. Never infer hydrological association solely from spatial intersection.

Geometry retains coordinate and part order. Do not silently reverse, simplify, clip or repair it. Record necessary transformations, including source geometry export and reprojection. Orientation 1/2 asserts first-to-last order relative to flow; for MultiLineString it also asserts parts are in connected flow order with each part consistently oriented. Otherwise use 0. Connectivity and directed node references remain authoritative regardless of orientation; 0 is not a failure.

docs.title: Source nodes
docs.text:
The optional river_nodes family has no flow graph or topology declaration. Required node fields are nonnull id: int64, level: int16, source_namespace: string, source_id: string, bbox of the catchment struct type, and geometry: binary (Point WKB in EPSG:4326), plus nullable coarser_node_id: int64. Node IDs are positive and unique across node tiers; level is the nonnegative river tier. A coarser-node reference resolves at a strictly smaller level and means source-declared correspondence, not constituent membership. Keep source layers distinct even if coordinates and numeric source IDs match.

Nonnull river endpoint IDs resolve to nodes at that river's level. These references are the canonical incidence relation: incoming rivers have that downstream node; outgoing rivers have that upstream node. Preserve original incidence strings, ordering-dependent width shares, cross-tier reference columns, diagnostics and other typed attributes alongside it. Do not invent nodes for sources without them. No node reference may be nonnull when the node artifact is absent. Verify that source-supplied flow edges and endpoint incidence agree; sharing a node alone does not imply every possible incoming/outgoing river pair is a source flow edge.

docs.title: Flow connectivity
docs.text: Supplied flow graphs are acyclic. tree allows at most one downstream neighbor; dag allows splits and reconvergence without duplicating features. Each upstream ID denotes an edge from that feature to the row's feature at the same level. IDs resolve within the corresponding domain. Lists have no nulls, duplicates or self-links. Parent membership is not flow. Validate complete source edges before declaring conformance; a cycle cannot be excused by an anomaly note or removed silently. Acyclicity does not certify hydrological continuity.

docs.title: Typed meanings and source fidelity
docs.text:
HFX fixes structural fields, not a complete source attribute schema. Preserve useful source attributes, physical types, nulls and meanings. Explicitly approved lossless type mappings may change physical width while preserving exact values and nulls; retain original per-source declarations and document the mapping. TDX catchment streamID widens int32 to int64 under this rule. Document retained, renamed, transformed and omitted fields; a collision with an HFX structural name requires an explicit source-column rename map in provenance, not value replacement. Retain source field/schema metadata where applicable; update geometry metadata for actual delivered CRS and bounds rather than carrying stale projected metadata.

The optional categorical_columns array binds a dictionary to one scalar column:

{
  "artifact": "rivers.parquet", "column": "level", "physical_type": "int16",
  "codes": [{"code": 0, "meaning": "segment"}, {"code": 1, "meaning": "reach"}],
  "null_meaning": "not permitted"
}

artifact is an exact local artifact path, column a top-level field name. physical_type is one of string, bool, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, matching the Arrow field's logical scalar type (dictionary encoding, if present, does not change this type). Codes are unique, nonnull JSON values of that type; integer parsing must preserve full precision. Every observed nonnull value has one nonempty string meaning. null_meaning is a required nonempty description of null interpretation, even for nonnullable fields. At most one dictionary binds each artifact/column pair. Dictionaries define dataset semantics, not cross-dataset equivalence or Arrow compression. Level descriptions supplement HFX ordering, never replace parents/edges. A source termination_kind may use this mechanism; no universal outlet vocabulary is required. Preserve underspecified source codes with an explicit uncertainty description.

Subsets retain external source edge identities in source columns and document which edges were cut, in each direction; structural graph references still resolve within the delivered subset. Never turn a known cut into a source terminal.

Select whole sub-basins approximating land draining to a target.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fabric HydroFabric

Open HFX fabric supplying catchments and upstream connectivity.

required target BaseGeometry | Targets

EPSG:4326 geometry, or a dictionary of named geometries or list for a batch. A multipart geometry is one target. Regions include boundary intersections. A point on a shared boundary belongs to the smallest supplied catchment ID; river associations do not determine ownership.

Nonnegative catchment level, selected explicitly without fallback.

1 n_jobs int

1

Type Description list or BatchResult

Whole intersecting units and their inclusive upstream closure. An empty geometry succeeds with an empty list. Batch slots preserve input order; dictionary keys are names, while list entries get new UUID names on each call. Duplicate geometries remain independent targets.

Type Description OperationError

selection.invalid_target for invalid geometry, selection.no_coverage for a nonempty target without coverage, or selection.connectivity_unavailable for unsupplied connectivity. Batches retain these failures as issues with None result slots.

ValueError

Invalid level or worker count, or a flow relationship crossing levels.

TypeError

Invalid target type or batch names.

Notes

This is whole-unit selection, not exact-point raster delineation. Returned vectors survive fabric closure. Integrity, configuration and unexpected failures propagate even in batches; they are not empty selections.

Trace incoming native D8 flow inside a complete vector mask.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fabric HydroFabric

Open fabric supplying the native direction/accumulation pair.

required target Point | None

Nonempty point in EPSG:4326 covered by the mask. Omit for a selection batch, which carries its own target geometries.

None subbasins Sequence[Subbasin] | BatchResult[list[Subbasin]] | None

Whole source units forming one mask, or a selection BatchResult. Mutually exclusive with footprint. Batch identity, order and prior issues are preserved; failed slots are not retried.

None footprint BaseGeometry | None

Nonempty Polygon or MultiPolygon in EPSG:4326, used as one mask. Supply exactly one mask form. Batch footprints come from subbasins.

None window_size int

Positive odd search width in native cells around the cell containing the target. Size 1 permits no move beyond that cell. Selects the highest valid accumulation inside the mask, breaking ties by source row then column. Both bands must be valid for outlet selection.

3 n_jobs int

Batch worker limit: 1 is sequential, -1 uses available CPU capacity, and positive values bound worker-owned readers.

1

Returns:

Type Description GranularRefinement or FootprintRefinement or BatchResult

Contributions for sub-basin input or one footprint for geometry input, plus the selected native outlet cell and materialized raster subsets. Empty source pieces are omitted. Both forms trace the same combined mask; merging granular contributions yields the footprint result.

Raises:

Type Description OperationError

refinement.point_required for a nonpoint or empty point geometry, refinement.empty_mask for an empty or nonpolygon mask, refinement.outside_mask when the point is not covered, refinement.missing_rasters for an absent raster pair, refinement.no_coverage for inadequate raster coverage, or refinement.no_outlet when the local search has no valid masked cell. Batches retain these failures as issues with None slots.

ValueError

Invalid window/worker count or mutually incompatible mask arguments. Integrity and unexpected errors also propagate, including in batches.

TypeError

A single call omits target.

Notes

Assumes the whole vector mask equals the raster watershed at the terminal unit outlet, and that the requested point drains to that outlet. Execution does not verify this scientific equivalence. The default local search is a practical choice, not a universal optimum; larger windows can switch branches.

Mask cells use GDAL center-based rasterization. Reverse D8 tracing spans the entire mask and needs only valid direction, not valid accumulation; zero and signed negative directions are terminal. Paths cannot leave the mask. Native direction pointers are never warped. Selected cell polygons are transformed to EPSG:4326 and clipped to the vector mask, then partitioned at source boundaries for granular output. No hole filling is applied. Materialized vectors survive fabric closure; perform source-dependent operations and export within the fabric context.

docs.title: pourpoint.select_rivers(*, fabric: HydroFabric, target: BaseGeometry | Subbasin | SubbasinContribution | Sequence[Subbasin | SubbasinContribution], level: int = 1, include_downstream: bool = False) -> RiverNetwork
docs.text:
Select river portions inside one combined footprint.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fabric HydroFabric

Open fabric supplying rivers and their relationships.

required target BaseGeometry | Subbasin | SubbasinContribution | Sequence[Subbasin | SubbasinContribution]

EPSG:4326 polygonal geometry, sub-basin/contribution, or collection of parts forming one footprint. Internal part boundaries do not limit flow; this collection is not a batch of independent targets.

required level int

Nonnegative river level, independent of catchment levels. No fallback or inferred correspondence between catchment and river tiers is used.

1 include_downstream bool

Extend along every supplied outgoing continuation, including splits and reconvergence. Features are deduplicated by source ID. Partial boundary features require unambiguous orientation to retain downstream linework.

False

Returns:

Type Description RiverNetwork

Selected portions with original identities, attributes, directed relationships and supplied nodes. Source quantities are not recomputed. Empty footprints or no intersecting rivers give an empty network when the river family and its relationship data are supplied. Materialized results survive closure.

Raises:

Type Description OperationError

rivers.unavailable when the river family is absent; rivers.connectivity_unavailable when extension needs a missing downstream_ids column in supplied relationship data; rivers.ambiguous_direction when a partial feature cannot be oriented from supplied orientation or endpoint nodes.

KeyError

River relationship data are not declared, even for an empty footprint or no matching rivers. Missing referenced source IDs also raise.

ValueError

Invalid level, nonpolygonal nonempty footprint, or downstream flow crossing river levels. Integrity errors propagate rather than producing a partial network.

Notes

Clipping creates endpoints, not natural outlets. Retained relationship references outside the selection must not be interpreted as missing flow or source-described termination. No mainstem is inferred from node incidence.

docs.title: pourpoint.QGISBundle
docs.text:
Build a portable QGIS folder incrementally without hydrological computation.

Notes

Add methods retain data and return this builder for chaining. write creates a new folder with a relative-reference project, GeoPackage and native-grid GeoTIFFs; it never replaces an existing path. No merging, delineation or river tracing is performed implicitly. Perform source-dependent export inside the fabric context; current raster subsets already contain materialized arrays.

Scalar source fields become ordinary vector columns. Reserved-name collisions gain source_ prefixes; source_metadata.attribute_columns records names. Rich values, original WKB and Arrow schemas/metadata are losslessly retained as IPC streams in source_arrow. Result locations are WGS84 WKB in result_metadata, alongside provenance; these are not extra map layers.
